As a Motorola 360 user, they need to get thinner. I can't wear long sleeve shirts and some of my jackets because they either bunch up to the side of the watch forcing it uncomfortably against your hand, or they can't be retracted easily to read the screen.

For me personally, it all revolves around battery life. The one thing keeping me from ditching my Eco-Drive watch for a smartwatch is that I never have to take it off; it never needs to be charged/new battery. I know that if I have to constantly remove a wearable and recharge it, I will forget it and it will hold down my desk/bedside table for days on end. My Bluetooth hands-free device was always lost or charging somewhere.

I love wearable devices, but I will refrain from saying they will become a mainstay in my life until we can really improve battery tech. If tech improves as fast as I hope it does, they may become outdated before they really ever catch on as more than the current novelty item that I see them as now.

I think that we'll have a "core" device, probably the size of either a current phone or something that can fit in a watch. Everything else we will use, be it a watch, desktop, tablet, or lenses will be nothing but screens. We'll see the same info, but only need one physical device. You'll be able to sit down at home and your TV will automatically know you're in the room and display your "core" system for you. Cars will automatically have your playlists and recent map history, because you've just carried it with you.

Though, I think that's 10-20 years away from being more than a concept.
